classification.description: The verdict the source gives, in its own word. `malicious`, `suspicious` and `benign` are the words MISP reads as a verdict; anything else, including `unknown`, is recorded as the source said it and read as no opinion.

first-seen.description: First time the source saw the value on this list, or first observation behind the verdict

last-seen.description: Last time the source saw the value on this list, or most recent observation behind the verdict

link.description: Link to the source's own report for this value

list-name.description: The specific list or zone the value was found on, where the source publishes more than one (e.g. a DNSBL zone)

score.description: How sure the source is, on its own scale. State the scale in `text` where it is not 0-100

source.description: The service or list that gave the verdict

text.description: Anything the source said that the fields above do not hold, including the scale a non-standard score is on

description: What an outside source thinks of a value: a classification, a score, or both. The generic counterpart to the vendor verdict objects (abuseipdb, greynoise-ip, crowdsec-ip-context, virustotal-report), for the sources that do not warrant a template of their own - blocklists, DNSBLs, scam lists - and a place for vendors to state a verdict beside their own richer object.
name: reputation
